mainTopic: Why must a שליח say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם? Can רבה (not experts in לשמה) and רבא (no witnesses available) each explain the משניות, and what is the practical difference between them?
overview: The amud opens by finishing a suggestion: maybe the argument in the משנה is the same as the argument between רבה and רבא. That argument is about why a שליח must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. רבה says the reason is that people overseas are not experts in writing a גט לשמה. רבא says it is because witnesses are not around to confirm the signatures. The גמרא rejects the suggestion, because each of them can explain the משנה his own way. Next the גמרא reads an inference out of the משנה's words 'from region to region overseas.' It gives two versions of this challenge, one against רבה and one against רבא, and answers both. Along the way it explains that within ארץ ישראל witnesses are easy to find, first because of the festival pilgrims and later because of fixed courts. The case of the two districts of עססיות seems to fit only רבא. The גמרא answers that רבה holds רבא's reason too and simply adds his own. It then names two cases where they really differ: two people bringing the גט, and a גט brought within one region overseas. Finally, the גמרא quotes a משנה about a שליח who 'is unable to say' the declaration and starts to ask what those words mean.

steps.title: Finishing the suggestion that the argument depends on the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its suggestion. The תנא קמא would hold the reason is לשמה, and people in ארץ ישראל are experts. The later רבנן would hold the reason is the lack of witnesses, and witnesses traveling from ארץ ישראל are also rare.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these people (in ארץ ישראל) are knowledgeable. And the other master holds the reason is that witnesses are not available to confirm the גט, and witnesses from ארץ ישראל are also not common. Shall we say that is the argument?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an attempt to show that the argument in the משנה is really about the reason behind בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the לשמה reason, a גט leaving ארץ ישראל needs no declaration, because people there know the laws. Under the witnesses reason, it does need one, since witnesses from ארץ ישראל are just as hard to find overseas. This would make the argument between רבה and רבא an older argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: They are learned; they know the laws
To confirm it (to verify the signatures on the גט)

phrases.english: and these are learned;
phrases.notes: "These" means the people in ארץ ישראל, who know how to write a גט לשמה.

phrases.english: and the other master holds
it is because there are no witnesses available to confirm it,
and these too are not commonly found?
phrases.notes: Witnesses from ארץ ישראל are also hard to find overseas, so the declaration would still be needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר סָבַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proposal begun before this passage.
steps.raayaObject: That the argument between רבה (לשמה) and רבא (witnesses) is already an argument between תנאים in the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תנא קמא does not require the מוליך to make the declaration, while the later רבנן do.

steps.title: Both רבה and רבא can explain the משנה their own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבה can explain the משנה according to his reason, and רבא can explain it according to his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה explains the משנה according to his own reasoning, and רבא explains it according to his own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion and sets up the next move. Each אמורא will explain the משנה in a way that fits his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof fails if each side can read the משנה so that it does not contradict him. So the argument in the משנה does not have to be about the reason at all. The גמרא now shows how each one does this.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רבא are two different אמוראים with very similar names. Here רבה holds the לשמה reason, and רבא holds the witnesses reason.

phrases.english: Rabba explains it according to his reasoning,
and Rava explains it according to his reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, וְרָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attempted proof from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole claim that the משנה's argument is about the reason for the declaration.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each אמורא can explain the משנה so that it fits his own view, so the משנה proves nothing.

steps.title: רבה: everyone agrees on לשמה, but they argue about a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה, both sides in the משנה agree the reason is that people are not experts in לשמה. They argue only about whether to make a גזירה on the מוליך because of the מביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה explains it his way: everyone agrees the reason is that people are not experts in writing a גט לשמה. Here they argue about a decree requiring the one who takes a גט out (מוליך) to make the declaration, because of the one who brings a גט in (מביא).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows how the משנה fits his view. He moves the argument from 'what is the reason' to 'did חז"ל make an extra decree.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone holds the לשמה reason, then by strict law only the מביא needs to make the declaration. The only question left is whether חז"ל also required the מוליך, so people would not mix up the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Experts in writing the גט for her specific sake
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
One who takes a גט from ארץ ישראל overseas
One who brings a גט from overseas to ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction. מביא means bringing the גט INTO ארץ ישראל from overseas. מוליך means taking it OUT of ארץ ישראל to overseas.

phrases.english: Rabba explains it according to his reasoning:
that everyone agrees
it is because they are not experts in writing it for her sake,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בִּגְזֵירַת מוֹלִיךְ אַטּוּ מֵבִיא קָמִיפַּלְגִי –
phrases.english: and here they argue about a decree on one who takes out because of one who brings in –

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבה's half of the rejection announced in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different point (a גזירה instead of the reason).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue about the reason for the declaration.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree on the לשמה reason. They argue only about the גזירה of מוליך because of מביא.

steps.title: The two sides of the גזירה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא does not make the גזירה, so the מוליך need not say the declaration. The later רבנן do make it, so the מוליך must say it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds we do not decree on the one who takes a גט out because of the one who brings one in. The later רבנן hold we do make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what each side in the משנה holds, according to רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept that only the מביא strictly needs the declaration. The later רבנן worry that people will see a מוליך skip it and then think a מביא can skip it too. So they require it from both.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
Because of; out of concern for
The later Rabbis (the חכמים at the end of the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, everyone holds the reason is לשמה. The argument in the משנה is only whether חז"ל decreed that the מוליך must also say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, because of the מביא.

phrases.english: for the first tanna holds:
we do not decree on one who takes out because of one who brings in.
And the later Rabbis hold:
we do decree on one who takes out because of one who brings in.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: לָא גָּזְרִינַן מוֹלִיךְ אַטּוּ מֵבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details of רבה's explanation from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא does not decree on the מוליך because of the מביא. The later רבנן do.

steps.title: How רבא explains the משנה by his own reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone in the משנה agrees the reason is that no witnesses are available. The later רבנן are not arguing; they are only explaining what the תנא קמא meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא explains the משנה his way: everyone agrees the reason is that there are no witnesses around to confirm the גט. The later רבנן did not come to argue. They came to explain the reason of the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא, like רבה, can fit the משנה into his own reason, so the משנה cannot decide between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא there is no real argument in the משנה at all. Everyone holds the reason is that witnesses are hard to find. The later רבנן simply spell out that someone bringing a גט from ארץ ישראל to overseas must also say it, which the תנא קמא already agreed to.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains the source according to his own reasoning
To confirm it, meaning to confirm the signatures on the גט
The later רבנן, the second opinion in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבה and רבא can explain the משנה. רבה reads it as a real argument about a גזירה. רבא reads it as no argument at all, just an explanation.

phrases.english: And רבא explains it according to his own reasoning:
that everyone agrees
it is because there are no witnesses available to confirm it,
and the later רבנן

phrases.aramaic: לְפָרוֹשֵׁי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא הוּא דְּאָתוּ.
phrases.english: came only to explain the reasoning of the תנא קמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to steps 3-4: after showing how רבה reads the משנה, the גמרא shows how רבא reads it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the apparent argument is really one opinion being explained
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two opinions in the משנה seemed to argue about the reason, one side matching רבה and the other matching רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא, everyone agrees the reason is the lack of witnesses, and the later רבנן only explain the תנא קמא.

steps.title: A line in the משנה seems to fit רבא and challenge רבה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a גט brought from one region to another overseas needs the declaration. That implies within the same region it does not. This fits רבא (witnesses are close by) but is hard for רבה (people overseas are still not experts in לשמה).
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: one who brings a גט from region to region within a country overseas must say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence.' This implies that within the same overseas region, he does not need to. This works for רבא, but it is difficult for רבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה and draws an inference from it that seems to prove רבא right and challenge רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is witnesses, then inside one region witnesses can easily be found, so no declaration is needed. But if the reason is that people do not know the laws of לשמה, that is just as true inside one overseas region, so the declaration should still be needed. The inference seems to go against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A country overseas, outside ארץ ישראל
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two names: רבה (with a ה) holds the reason is that people are not experts in לשמה. רבא (with an א) holds the reason is that witnesses are not available. This challenge is against רבה.

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה:
One who brings a גט from region to region
within a country overseas
must say:
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence."

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּאוֹתָהּ מְדִינָה בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם – לֹא צָרִיךְ.
phrases.english: This implies: within the same region overseas, he does not need to.
According to רבא, this works well,
but according to רבה, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source failed to decide between רבה and רבא, the גמרא tries a new line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason that the declaration is needed because people overseas are not experts in לשמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies no declaration is needed within one overseas region. Lack of expertise in לשמה would still apply there, so רבה's reason does not explain that leniency.

steps.title: רבה reads the inference differently
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the inference from 'region to region overseas' is not about one region overseas. It is about region to region within ארץ ישראל, where no declaration is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say the inference is 'within the same overseas region he does not need to.' Rather, say the inference is 'from region to region within ארץ ישראל, he does not need to.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by changing what the inference from the משנה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'overseas' are what the inference contrasts with, not the words 'region to region.' So the משנה is implying: overseas you must say it even between regions, but in ארץ ישראל you do not. That fits רבה, since people in ארץ ישראל are experts in לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say (do not read it that way)

phrases.english: Do not say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּאוֹתָהּ מְדִינָה בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם – לֹא צָרִיךְ,
phrases.english: "This implies: within the same region overseas, he does not need to,"
rather, say:

phrases.aramaic: מִמְּדִינָה לִמְדִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל – לֹא צָרִיךְ.
phrases.english: "From region to region within ארץ ישראל, he does not need to."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבה from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the inference drawn from the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that within one overseas region no declaration is needed, which goes against רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה implies that within ארץ ישראל, even from region to region, no declaration is needed, which fits רבה.

steps.title: Why infer something the משנה already says openly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבה's answer: the משנה already says clearly that one who brings a גט within ארץ ישראל does not need the declaration. So why would we need an inference to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches this explicitly: one who brings a גט within ארץ ישראל does not need to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 7 by pointing out that its lesson is already stated openly elsewhere in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה does not usually teach the same rule twice. If the ארץ ישראל rule is already stated plainly, it seems pointless to read it into the line about overseas regions as well. That makes רבה's reading look weak.

phrases.english: But the משנה teaches this explicitly:
One who brings a גט within ארץ ישראל
does not need to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given for רבה in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 7, that the overseas line implies no declaration is needed within ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already states that rule openly, so reading it into another line would repeat it for no reason.

steps.title: The inference adds that it is fine even from the outset
steps.stepSummary: From the open statement alone we might think the leniency in ארץ ישראל is only after the fact. The inference teaches that the שליח need not say it even from the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we had only that line, I would have thought it applies only after the fact, but not from the outset. So the inference teaches us that even from the outset he does not need to say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the inference is not a repeat. It teaches something new about the ארץ ישראל rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Does not need to say' could mean only that the גט is still valid if he did not say it (דיעבד). The inference, set side by side with 'must say' overseas, shows the rule is on the same level: in ארץ ישראל he need not say it at all, even לכתחילה. So רבה's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact, once it already happened

steps.whatToRemember: רבה survives the challenge: the משנה's line about overseas regions implies that in ארץ ישראל no declaration is needed, even לכתחילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a rule that seems to be repeated is really adding a detail, such as moving from דיעבד to לכתחילה.

phrases.english: If we had only that line,
I would have thought
that this applies only after the fact,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if he already brought it without saying it, the גט is still good.

phrases.english: but not from the outset,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8 and keeps רבה's reading from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the second source adds new information (דיעבד versus לכתחילה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the open statement alone, the leniency in ארץ ישראל might apply only after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inference teaches that in ארץ ישראל the declaration is not needed even from the outset.

steps.title: A second version of the challenge, this time against רבא
steps.stepSummary: Some read the משנה's inference as 'region to region within ארץ ישראל needs no declaration.' That fits רבה but is hard for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raise the objection this way: the משנה implies that one who brings a גט from region to region within ארץ ישראל does not need to say the declaration. This fits רבה, but it is difficult for רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the challenge from the same words of the משנה. This time the challenge is against רבא instead of רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the משנה's words 'from region to region overseas' imply that region to region within ארץ ישראל needs no declaration. For רבה that is easy, because people in ארץ ישראל know about לשמה. For רבא it is a problem, because the issue is finding witnesses, and witnesses from a different region in ארץ ישראל are not close by either.

keyTerms.meaning: Some raise the objection this way (a second version of the challenge)
It fits / it works out well

steps.confusionAlert: In the first version (Step 6), the inference was 'within one region overseas,' and it was hard for רבה. In this version, the inference is 'region to region in ארץ ישראל,' and it is hard for רבא. Same משנה, opposite target.

phrases.english: And some raise the objection like this:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִמְּדִינָה לִמְדִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל – לֹא צָרִיךְ.
phrases.english: This implies that from region to region within Eretz Yisrael, he does not need to say it.
For Rabba, this fits well; for Rava, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the Step 6 challenge, now aimed at רבא instead of רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that the reason for the declaration is that witnesses are not available
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה implies no declaration is needed from region to region in ארץ ישראל, the reason cannot be a lack of witnesses. Witnesses from another region are not nearby, so רבא would require the declaration there.

steps.title: Changing the inference to one region overseas
steps.stepSummary: Do not infer 'region to region in ארץ ישראל.' Infer instead that within one region overseas no declaration is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say the משנה implies that region to region within ארץ ישראל needs no declaration. Rather, say it implies that within one region overseas, no declaration is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by changing what the משנה's words imply. The inference is now about staying within one region overseas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from region to region overseas' can be contrasted with 'within the same region overseas.' Within one region the witnesses are close by, which is exactly רבא's reason. So the inference now supports רבא instead of hurting him.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say this... rather, say that (reading the source a different way)

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא: מִמְּדִינָה לִמְדִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל – לֹא צָרִיךְ,
phrases.english: Do not say: from region to region within Eretz Yisrael he does not need to,
rather, say: this implies that within one region
in a country overseas, he does not need to.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא מִמְּדִינָה לִמְדִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא צָרִיךְ אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Step 10 challenge against רבא by reading the inference differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the משנה's wording implies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's wording implies that within ארץ ישראל, region to region, no declaration is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's wording only implies that within one region overseas no declaration is needed, which fits רבא.

steps.title: Then would region to region in ארץ ישראל need the declaration?
steps.stepSummary: If the inference is only about one region overseas, then region to region in ארץ ישראל would need the declaration. If so, the משנה should have said 'region to region' with no mention of overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about bringing a גט from region to region within ארץ ישראל? Does he need to say it? If so, let the משנה just say 'One who brings a גט from region to region,' without mentioning overseas!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. According to רבא's logic, ארץ ישראל region to region should also need the declaration, so why did the משנה mention overseas at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבא's reason (no witnesses nearby) applies to any move between regions, it should apply in ארץ ישראל too. Then the word 'overseas' in the משנה would be extra. The משנה could have just said 'region to region' and covered both places.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach (the משנה should have said)

phrases.english: But from region to region within Eretz Yisrael,
what is the law? Does he need to?!
Let it teach: 'One who brings from region to region,' without specifying!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִמְּדִינָה לִמְדִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאי צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the Step 11 answer by pointing to the extra word 'overseas' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 11 reading, and with it רבא's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If region to region in ארץ ישראל also requires the declaration, the משנה's mention of 'overseas' is unnecessary. It should have just said 'region to region.'

steps.title: Pilgrims make witnesses easy to find in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Even for רבא, region to region in ארץ ישראל needs no declaration. Because people travel to ירושלים for the festivals, witnesses are easy to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, from region to region within ארץ ישראל he also does not need to say it. Since there are people going up to ירושלים for the festivals, witnesses are easily found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא agrees ארץ ישראל needs no declaration even between regions. The reason still fits his view: witnesses can easily be found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason is about whether witnesses are available to confirm the גט. In ארץ ישראל, people from every region meet when they go up to ירושלים for the festivals, so witnesses from another region are easy to reach. That explains why the משנה mentioned overseas: only there are witnesses from another region hard to find.

keyTerms.meaning: Pilgrims who go up to ירושלים for the three festivals

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רבא's reason (no witnesses available) survives. Within one region overseas, witnesses are close by. Within ארץ ישראל, even between regions, the festival pilgrims make witnesses easy to find. So inside the overseas lands, the declaration is needed only when the גט moves from one region to another.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבא's view can explain every detail of the משנה's wording, including why it limited the rule to overseas.

phrases.english: Really, from region to region within Eretz Yisrael
he also does not need to,
because since there are those who go up for the festivals,
they are commonly found.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם מִמְּדִינָה לִמְדִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי לֹא צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by explaining why ארץ ישראל is different even under רבא's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that a real-world fact makes רבא's reason apply differently in ארץ ישראל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבא, region to region in ארץ ישראל should need the declaration, which would make 'overseas' an extra word in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבא, no declaration is needed in ארץ ישראל either, because the festival pilgrims make witnesses available. So 'overseas' is a necessary word in the משנה.

steps.title: What about after the בית המקדש was destroyed?
steps.stepSummary: The answer about pilgrims going to ירושלים only works while the בית המקדש stands. After it is destroyed, how are witnesses easy to find?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works well when the בית המקדש is standing. But when the בית המקדש is not standing, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from the last step. Pilgrims only went up to ירושלים while the בית המקדש stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 we said that within ארץ ישראל witnesses are easy to find because everyone goes up to ירושלים for the festivals. Without a בית המקדש there are no pilgrimages. So the reason seems to disappear, but the leniency for ארץ ישראל still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine (only in one case)
What is there to say? (asking for an answer to a problem)

phrases.english: This works out well when the Temple is standing;
when the Temple is not standing,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The pilgrimage reason for why witnesses are easy to find in ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pilgrimage reason depends on the בית המקדש. After the Temple is destroyed the reason is gone, yet the ruling still applies.

steps.title: Fixed courts keep witnesses available
steps.stepSummary: Even without the בית המקדש there are permanent courts that everyone goes to, so witnesses are still easy to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there are courts that sit in fixed places, witnesses are often found there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: permanent courts take the place of the pilgrimages. People keep traveling to them, so witnesses can be found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real point is that people from different places meet. The festivals did that before, and fixed בתי דינין do it now. So רבא's reason, that witnesses are easy to find, still holds in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: That are fixed, set in a permanent place

phrases.english: Since there are courts that are fixed —
they are commonly found.
phrases.notes: 'They' means witnesses who can confirm the signatures on the גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the original reason with another reason that has the same effect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the בית המקדש, nothing brings people together, so witnesses would be hard to find.
steps.terutzMaskana: Permanent courts bring people together, so witnesses are still found.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the leniency in ארץ ישראל is all about witnesses being easy to find: once through the festivals, and later through fixed courts.

steps.title: The case of the two districts of עססיות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who requires the declaration even from district to district. רבי יצחק explains that this was about a city whose two districts did not let people cross between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, even from one district to another. And רבי יצחק said: there was a city in ארץ ישראל called עססיות. It had two districts that were strict with each other. That is why they had to say 'from district to district.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and an explanation of it. This sets up the next step, which will test it against רבה and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would going from one district to another need the declaration? רבי יצחק explains that the two districts would not let people move between them. So people from one side could not be found on the other side. That points to the reason being witnesses, which is רבא's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A district under its own governor
Name of a city in ארץ ישראל
Were strict with each other (did not allow crossing)

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: We learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even from district to district.
phrases.notes: He means the שליח must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' even here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There was one city in Eretz Yisrael
and Asasiyyot was its name,
and there were two districts in it
that were strict with each other,
phrases.notes: The two sides would not let people cross over, so people from one side were not found on the other.

phrases.english: therefore they needed to say
'from district to district.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new test of the two opinions using a משנה
steps.raayaObject: That the declaration depends on whether witnesses are available
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, as explained by רבי יצחק

steps.title: This fits רבא but is hard for רבה
steps.stepSummary: The districts case is about witnesses who cannot cross over. That fits רבא, but רבה said the reason is knowing the law of לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא this works well. According to רבה it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the districts case to challenge רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the districts case the people of both districts live in ארץ ישראל and know the law of לשמה equally well. The only problem is that witnesses cannot cross. רבה's reason, knowing the law, does not explain why a declaration is needed here.

phrases.english: According to Rava it works well,
according to Rabba it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the source from step 16 against רבה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason (the declaration is needed because overseas they are not experts in לשמה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both districts are in ארץ ישראל, so knowing the law is not the issue. Only the lack of witnesses explains the rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names: רבה (with a ה) says the reason is knowing the law of לשמה; רבא (with an א) says the reason is finding witnesses.

steps.title: רבה also accepts רבא's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבה agrees with רבא's reason about witnesses. He just adds his own reason about לשמה on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה also holds the reason of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה does not argue on the witnesses reason. He holds both reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה never denied that a lack of witnesses requires the declaration. He holds that witnesses are one reason, and not knowing לשמה is a second one. So the districts case fits him too.

phrases.english: Rabba holds the view of Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that one opinion includes the other's reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה only holds the לשמה reason, so the districts case is hard for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה holds both reasons, witnesses and לשמה, so the districts case fits him too.

steps.title: So what is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: If רבה accepts רבא's reason, the גמרא asks where they actually disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between רבה and רבא. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבה holds רבא's reason plus one more, they seem to agree almost everywhere. The גמרא wants a case where the extra reason of רבה changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: Rather, what is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer of step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where רבה and רבא would rule differently

steps.title: The difference: two people bring the גט
steps.stepSummary: The difference is when two people bring the גט. רבא needs no declaration, since they are already two witnesses. רבה still needs the declaration because of לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when two people bring the גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case where they disagree: two people bring the גט from overseas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people bringing the גט can confirm it themselves, so for רבא there is no witness problem and no declaration is needed. For רבה there is still the worry that overseas they don't know the law of לשמה. So the declaration is still needed for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Written for the sake of this specific woman

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the declaration is only about witnesses. רבה: it is about witnesses and also about לשמה. So when two people bring the גט, רבא needs no declaration, but רבה still does.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where two people brought it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When two people bring the גט: according to רבא no declaration is needed, according to רבה it is still needed because of לשמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows exactly what each reason adds. It makes clear that רבה's view requires more than רבא's.

steps.title: A second difference: carrying a גט within one overseas region
steps.stepSummary: Another case where רבה and רבא differ is a גט brought from place to place inside the same region overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, the difference is when the גט is brought within one region overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question of Step 19, where רבה and רבא actually disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside one region, people who can confirm the signatures are close by, so רבא's worry about missing witnesses does not apply and no declaration is needed. רבה still requires the declaration, because the problem that people overseas do not know the law of לשמה is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: An overseas country, outside ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: There are two differences between רבה and רבא. The first is two people bringing the גט. The second is a גט brought within one overseas region. In both cases רבא needs no declaration, and רבה still needs it because of לשמה.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
within the same region in a country overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, בְּאוֹתָהּ מְדִינָה בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second practical difference, as an alternative to the two-agents case of Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do רבה and רבא differ in practice?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גט brought within a single overseas region. Signatures can be confirmed there, so רבא needs no declaration, but רבה still needs it for לשמה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a שליח who cannot make the declaration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if the שליח cannot say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, the גט can be confirmed through its signing witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: someone who brings a גט from overseas and cannot say 'it was written before me and signed before me' can rely on the witnesses signed on it, and the גט is confirmed through their signatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a משנה. This is setup for the discussion and challenge that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that there is another way to make the גט valid: confirming the signatures of its witnesses. The גמרא will look closely at the words 'he is unable to say' to learn something about the reason behind the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: It was written in my presence and signed in my presence
It is confirmed through its signers, by checking the witnesses' signatures

phrases.english: We learned: One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas,
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in the מסכת, on דף ט.

phrases.english: and he is unable to say
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,'
if there are witnesses on it,
it shall be confirmed through its signers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of differences and brings a new source that will be tested against the opinions of רבה and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח who cannot make the declaration can still have the גט confirmed through its signing witnesses.

steps.title: Asking what 'he is unable to say' means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that it already discussed this משנה and asked what the phrase 'he is unable to say' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: what does 'he is unable to say' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back its own earlier question about the משנה's wording. It is preparing to explain the phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would a שליח be unable to make the declaration? Knowing the exact case behind these words will show which reason for the declaration the משנה assumes.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it, meaning we raised a question about it

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is meant by 'and he is unable to say'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at one phrase from the משנה quoted in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What situation does the משנה mean when it says the שליח 'is unable to say' the declaration?
